source_review.notes: Checked current Linux socket-buffer, networking KAPI, page-pool, netmem, MSG_ZEROCOPY, checksum-offload, segmentation-offload, AF_XDP, XDP receive-metadata and device-memory TCP documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; kernel contracts, provider constraints, abstract ownership models, operational guidance and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked buffer, metadata, linear head, fragments, geometry, DMA state, owner, reference graph, charge, checksum and segmentation notation.
Reviewed linear and nonlinear length, allocation geometry, reference-domain, write-authority, accounting and bounded-queue relations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates byte geometry, logical packet length, mutable metadata, shared backing, DMA state, accounting ownership and protocol metadata.

evidence: Executed a 2,048-byte head allocation with 128 bytes headroom, 384 linear bytes, 1,536 bytes tailroom and two fragments of 700 and 900 bytes.
Confirmed nonlinear length 1,600, total packet length 1,984, two shared-data references, metadata-only mutation without copying and payload mutation requiring copying.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates geometry and one clone-write decision only; it implements no SKB, page pool, DMA, network driver, socket, kernel or packet.

evidence: Re-derived total length as linear head length plus nonlinear data and verified headroom plus linear length plus tailroom equals the head allocation.
Checked that mutation requires geometric coverage and write authority, while recycling requires absence of device and consumer ownership.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of Linux networking, reference counting, DMA or memory providers.

evidence: Reviewed zero and maximum lengths, headers crossing fragments, insufficient headroom, integer overflow, maximum fragment arrays, shared heads, unreadable backing and allocation failure.
Reviewed mapping failure, noncoherent synchronization, delayed zero-copy notifications, tiny-payload memory attacks, queue purge, late completion, reset, removal and page-pool shutdown.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Geometry, sharing, reference, DMA, notification, charge, queue, provider and teardown boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced allocation, receive-ring publication, DMA completion, SKB construction, cloning, queueing, transmit mapping, completion, destruction and recycling through explicit ownership states.
Verified checked geometry, private writable mutation, metadata invalidation, bounded accounting, one final release and quiescence before provider destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats metadata, byte backing, fragments, DMA mappings, sockets, user pages and memory providers as coupled but independently reference-counted resources.

evidence: Reviewed SKB geometry, fragments, clones, COW, pull and linearization, metadata, accounting, page pools, netmem, DMA, zero-copy sends, queues and teardown.
Constructed counterexamples for cloned-as-writable, mapped-as-device-owned, notification-as-peer-delivery, metadata-reference-as-data-reference and timeout-as-completion.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable buffer-lifetime obligations, not a formal proof of Linux, a driver, NIC, memory provider, protocol or application.

evidence: Audited uses of allocated, shared, writable, mapped, synchronized, queued, charged, completed, notified, destroyed and recycled.
Confirmed kernel interface rules, abstract models, recommendations, tests and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: DMA completion is not labeled protocol delivery, zero-copy notification is not labeled peer receipt and a surviving metadata object is not labeled exclusive byte ownership.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-073/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the network-buffer geometry model.
Reviewed required kernel, architecture, memory-provider, driver, device, offload, queue, workload, fault and instrumentation evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one geometry and clone-write example only; it provides no evidence for Linux SKBs, page pools, DMA correctness, zero-copy completion, teardown safety or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed network buffers as two interacting graphs: byte geometry and resource ownership, joined by write authority, metadata validity, accounting and completion.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current Linux buffer mechanisms as implementable concerns, including fragment-safe access, COW, page recycling, DMA lifetime, bounded charging, zero-copy notification and shutdown containment. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from representation and geometry through sharing, transformation, metadata, accounting, backing providers, DMA, zero copy, overload and teardown, followed by explicit invariants, trade-offs, failure modes, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux networking, network-driver, NIC-vendor, memory-provider, protocol, performance, security, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
